title: Biomechanics of the lead straight punch and related indexes between sanda fighters and boxers from the perspective of cross-border talent transfer
retraction_or_correction_status: no retraction or correction recorded in OpenAlex at accessed_at
notes: cited_by_count 18 at harvest; a citation count is a measure of attention, not of correctness
methodology: Vicon 3D capture, two Kistler platforms and an instrumented target; lead straight punch compared between boxers and Sanda athletes across velocity, force and lower-limb indices.
main_findings: Peak punch velocity and contact velocity differed significantly between the two trained groups - style of training, not fitness, moves the numbers.
Differences also in peak impulse, peak strength, relative strength and rate of force development.
limitations: cross-sectional comparison of two trained populations
talent-transfer framing; not a controlled intervention

quoted_evidence.quote: Significant differences in the peak punch velocity and contact velocity were found between the two groups

project_implications: Evidence that a style is expressible as a different force-time curve for the SAME named punch - which is what our per-fighter move profiles would need if they are ever more than a damage scalar.
